lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-14 from the sm75-marlin worktree (pin 711b6898c46c6e99 per MEMORY.md 2026-09-06). (1) Layer structure: vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py, Qwen3_5DecoderLayer (lines 113-196) picks per config.layer_types either QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention ("linear_attention") or Qwen3NextAttention ("full_attention") - 24 GDN + 8 full d256 layers on this host; every layer carries its own MLP, two RMSNorms, and (dense path) a TP allreduce via reduce_results. (2) Per-GDN-layer decode launches, forward_cuda (qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py lines 875-947): in_proj_qkvz MergedColumnParallelLinear + in_proj_ba (2 Marlin W4A16 GEMMs, both consuming only hidden_states, i.e. mutually independent), then the registered custom op torch.ops.vllm.qwen_gdn_attention_core (direct_register_custom_op, line 1949), then _output_projection: RMSNormGated + out_proj Marlin GEMM + allreduce. Inside the op, the decode-only fast path _forward_core_decode_non_spec (line 1634, armed by VLLM_ENABLE_FLA_PACKED_RECURRENT_DECODE, default True in vllm/envs.py line 129) runs exactly two kernels: causal_conv1d_update (vendored causal-conv op) and fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode. So ~6-7 launches per GDN layer, ~150-170 launches for 24 GDN layers per step [estimate; exact count pending the plan/0010 step-profile ledger]. (3) The state-update kernel is the vendored FLA Triton kernel (vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_recurrent.py lines 255-343): one launch fusing in-kernel gating (softplus/sigmoid of a,b with A_log,dt_bias), q/k L2-norm, the delta-rule state update, and output - NO tl.dot anywhere (pure outer-product FMA and row reductions, so the Triton >=3.3 FMA-fallback that plan/0007 flagged for chunked prefill is irrelevant to this decode kernel); grid (NV=cdiv(V,32), B*HV) with a (NV,HV,B) fallback when B*HV>65535, num_warps=1, num_stages=3, BV=min(next_pow2(V),32); state is read AND written in place (h0=ht) through ssm_state_indices indirection into the paged mamba cache - atomic-free, fixed-order, graph-replay-safe. (4) The fused CUDA alternative exists upstream but is out of reach: vllm/envs.py line 130 defaults VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL="cuda", and _fused_gdn_decode_unsupported_reason (qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py lines 512-540) requires current_platform.has_device_capability(80) plus BF16 model/conv-state - sm_75 auto-falls back to the Triton path with an info log. The fusion precedent is vLLM PR #51674 "Add fused CUDA post-conv MTP decode kernel for Qwen3.5 GDN" (fuses post-conv + gating + recurrent + norm chain into one kernel), with a BF16->float promotion numerics note in issue #51779 and an auto-select-without-fallback crash in issue #53462. (5) Serialization today: vLLM V1 executes all 32 layers sequentially on one stream inside the full/piecewise CUDA graph; GDN state updates serialize with full-attention layers by construction - there is no cross-layer overlap machinery in the engine, and the layer chain is a true data dependency (each layer's input is the previous layer's output), so the publishable overlap surface is intra-layer only. (6) Ecosystem: vLLM Qwen3-Next blog (2025-09-11) states the integration rationale - "Launching Triton kernels can incur significant CPU overheads that disproportionately affect decode-only batches. To overcome this, vLLM enables full CUDA graph mode by default" - and lists "further kernel optimizations for GatedDeltaNet layers" on the roadmap; the vLLM 25K-TPS blog (2026-08-06) ships a Blackwell GDN PREFILL kernel (FlashInfer #3001, 1.02-5.78x over FLA/Triton; prefill only, SM90/100) and race-fixed async scheduling (a CPU-side scheduling feature, not GPU overlap); FlashInfer release notes carry "KDA recurrent-decode kernels ... optimized for lower decode latency"; Kimi Linear (arXiv 2510.26692, 2025-10-30) is the 3:1 KDA:MLA hybrid sibling with FlashKDA CUTLASS kernels open-sourced by Moonshot [uncertain: exact FlashKDA release date, ~2026]. Gated DeltaNet paper arXiv 2412.06464 (2024-12-09); NVIDIA Gated DeltaNet-2 arXiv 2605.22791 (2026). Mamba-family decode precedent is the same two-small-kernels shape (causal_conv1d_update + selective_state_update, state-spaces/mamba). Negative finding: no published work found, as of 2026-09-14, that overlaps or fuses the linear-attention state update WITH neighboring GEMMs in decode; the published levers are launch-count reduction (fusion) and CPU-overhead elimination (graphs, async scheduling) [uncertain: absent-positive claim over the whole literature; searched hybrid scheduling, FLA/FlashQLA/FlashInfer surfaces, Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next serving notes].
lacuna.applicability: On this host the GDN decode route is pinned by hardware, not choice: the fused CUDA path requires cc>=8.0 (source-verified gating above), so sm_75 rides the vendored FLA Triton packed-recurrent kernel (FLA 0.4.2 post-NaN-fix per the constraint frame; #792 tail-chunk NaN class is the known hazard). Where GDN time goes per step, from structure: (a) the three Marlin GEMMs per layer are weight-streaming and sit inside the ~9 GiB/step/rank DRAM wall (~16.8 ms at 535 GB/s) - that component is shared with every layer and irreducible at W4A16; (b) the state DRAM traffic is negligible - fp32 ssm state at the GVA 32/16-class shape is 128x128x4 B x 16 heads/rank x 24 layers = ~25 MiB read + 25 MiB write = ~50 MiB/step = ~0.09 ms at the wall [arithmetic estimate pending exact head counts]; (c) the residue is small-kernel latency and launch/gap time: ~3 non-GEMM kernels x 24 layers x ~2-15 us each plus graph-node overhead, plausibly ~0.3-0.7 ms/step [uncertain: no host measurement yet; the #step-profile ledger is the instrument]. What overlaps with what today: nothing overlaps - one stream, sequential graph. What could overlap: (i) in_proj_qkvz and in_proj_ba are independent GEMMs and could ride two graph branches (graph-node-concurrency item; both bandwidth-bound so the gain is tail-fill only); (ii) conv-update + recurrent could fuse into one Triton kernel (halves the op's internal launches; the upstream CUDA kernel proves the fusion is legal, a Triton port is sm_75-clean since no tl.dot is involved); (iii) RMSNormGated can fold into the out_proj quant-fusion pass; (iv) deferred state write-back overlapping the next layer is theoretically possible (state is not consumed until the same layer's next step) but rhymes with a falsified lever class (see failure_modes) and is graph-hostile [uncertain]. The honest ceiling: GDN-specific structure cannot yield multi-ms alone; its value is 24x multiplication of any per-layer microsecond saving and its contribution to the launch-count total that graph-node surgery attacks.

design.mechanism: Two candidate surgeries, both behind the existing custom-op boundary so CUDA graphs and the scheduler are untouched. (A) Fused conv+recurrent Triton kernel: extend the vendored packed-decode kernel to also perform the depthwise causal-conv update - each (n,hv) CTA already loads q,k,v from mixed_qkv; instead read the conv_state slice for the head's q/k/v rows (width-1 columns), apply the conv weights + SiLU in-register, then run the existing gating/L2norm/state-update body, and write the new conv columns back through the same ssm_state_indices-style indirection (conv cache is indexed by the same non_spec_state_indices_tensor). Grid and launch config unchanged (num_warps=1, num_stages=3, BV=32). One kernel replaces two inside torch.ops.vllm.qwen_gdn_attention_core; numerics identical to the current pair (same op order per element; fp32 accumulators retained). Gate with the banked GDN oracle plan from research/lacunae/results/gdn-linear-attention-sm75.json (fp64 torch reference + fused_recurrent fp32 second reference; tail-chunk and gate-magnitude cases per FLA #792). (B) Graph-branch concurrency for the two input projections: in_proj_qkvz and in_proj_ba write disjoint output buffers from the same input; capture them as two parallel graph nodes on a fork/join (or pre-captured side stream) so the smaller GEMM's tail hides under the larger - belongs to the graph-node-concurrency item's machinery, priced by the same ledger. Optionally (C, doctrine-only): fold RMSNormGated into the out_proj input quant fusion if the compilation pass's fuse_norm_quant covers RMSNormGated on this pin [uncertain: pass coverage at this pin not verified].
design.failure_modes: (1) Pipelining-of-dependents is a falsified lever class on this host: KV pipelining measured NEGATIVE (host lacuna record), and the analogous split-state-writeback-and-overlap idea adds a launch plus a dependency edge to a chain that is already latency-bound - expect the same sign; do not spend a GPU window on it before the ledger prices launches. (2) Pure copy/glue fusion showed NO_DIFF on this host (half2 staging result): fusing the elementwise glue around the custom op is not expected to pay by itself; only the conv+recurrent merge (which removes a kernel boundary on the critical path, not just copies) is a candidate. (3) Over-split economics: the kernel's BV=32 (NV=4) split is already chosen; raising NV to shrink CTAs further would replicate the host's PPS-knee finding (PPS knee at 1-2; PPS1 halves workspace and combine reads) in miniature - more partials, more traffic, no latency win at 1-warp CTAs. (4) Numerics: any fusion touching the gates must keep the fp32 softplus/exp path - FLA #792 (NaN via exp(0-g) overflow on tail chunks, 0*inf) is the proven silent-corruption class on exactly this arithmetic, and Turing's fp16 recast makes inf intermediates likelier (no bf16 refuge); oracle-first discipline per the banked item. (5) Graph safety: the packed kernel's grid flip (B*HV>65535) is static in B - safe at captured B; any new kernel must likewise derive all indexing from captured tensors (ssm_state_indices indirection pattern), never from host-side per-step values. (6) 1-warp CTAs are latency-bound on state loads: at B=4 the grid is (4, 64)=256 CTAs - occupancy is not the constraint, dependent-load latency is, so num_stages/prefetch is the only kernel-side dial that can matter.
design.effort_estimate: (A) is kernel-lane 1-2 sessions: clone the vendored kernel, add the in-register conv update, oracle sweep, cuda-graph replay check, one gate-1 ladder row. (B) and (C) are engine-lane items under graph-node-concurrency; zero standalone kernel work. Total 1-2 sessions if the ledger prices GDN above ~1 ms; near-zero otherwise (doctrine-only).
design.priority_signal: AGAINST as a standalone multi-ms lever: the GDN residue is bounded by ~0.3-0.7 ms of small kernels [uncertain] plus launch gaps, and the GEMM component sits at the shared DRAM wall - neither moves committed rows alone given the sensitivity floor (only multi-ms per-step deltas move committed rows). FOR as a multiplier and ledger line: 24 layers multiply every saved microsecond; the same ledger row prices GDN for both this item and graph-node-concurrency; and the fused conv+recurrent kernel is unusually cheap and low-risk here because the decode kernel has no tl.dot (no FMA-fallback exposure) and the fusion precedent exists upstream in CUDA (PR #51674) proving legality. Net: schedule behind #step-profile; execute (A) only if the ledger shows GDN non-GEMM time (kernels + gaps) above ~1 ms/step, else record the ledger row and retire the item.
